title_en: 19-Year-Old Southwest Airlines Boeing 737 Loses #2 Engine After Takeoff, Declares Emergency
title_zh: 已有 19 年历史的西南航空波音 737 飞机起飞后失去 2 号发动机，宣布进入紧急状态
summary: N281WN the carrier's 500th 737 circled over the South Bay as pilots ran emergency checklists and prepared for a single‑engine return.
summary_zh: N281WN 该航空公司的第 500 架 737 飞机在南湾上空盘旋，飞行员执行紧急检查表并准备单引擎返航。
body_en: Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.
His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

A Southwest Airlines flight experienced an engine failure shortly after takeoff from John Wayne Airport-Orange County Airport (SNA) on Friday. This resulted in the 19-year-old Boeing 737-700 declaring an emergency and diverting to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). The flight, onboard one of the country's largest airlines, stopped its climb and squawked 7700 , the standard broadcast for a general emergency to air traffic control .
WN3396, was a scheduled service from SNA to Norman Y. Mineta San Jose International Airport (SJC), and during the emergency diverted to LAX, where the aircraft landed safely.

According to CodeThreeNews , the crew onboard confirmed to air traffic control that there were 97 souls onboard, and shortly after its departure from Santa Ana, the jet lost power to its #2 engine. The aircraft at the center of the incident carries registration N281WN and was the 500th Boeing 737 delivered to the airline. It has accumulated more than 19 years of active service for the Dallas-based operator .
Following the incident, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) released the following statement, obtained by the Los Angeles Times .
"Southwest Airlines Flight 3396 landed safely at Los Angeles International Airport around 12:25 p.m. local time after the crew reported an engine issue."
A Southwest spokesperson also confirmed the incident in a statement to Simple Flying on Friday.

"Southwest Airlines Flight 3396 diverted safely to Los Angeles International Airport after the Pilots received an engine-related maintenance indication while flying from John Wayne Airport to San Jose Mineta International Airport," they explained. "The Pilots followed established procedures and landed the aircraft uneventfully. We appreciate the professionalism of our Pilots and Flight Crew. Southwest will accommodate our Customers on another flights to San Jose. Nothing is more important to Southwest than the Safety of our Customers and Employees."
Aircraft Left Circling The Skies Of Los Angeles

Reviewing data from the Simple Flying Flight Tracker, WN3396 was scheduled to depart from Santa Ana at 11:35, for a quick one-hour flight north to San Jose. The plane eventually pushed back from the gate at 11:49, 14 minutes behind schedule.

After taking off in a north-easterly direction, the plane quickly turned southwest after experiencing the engine issue, and the jet turned southwest toward Los Angeles South Bay. Flight data shows that the plane never flew higher than 5,000 feet (1,524 meters). After 18 minutes over the Pacific Ocean, the aircraft was cleared to land at LAX, touching down safely on Runway 25L at 12:28 after a total flight time of 38 minutes.

Emergency services met the aircraft on arrival, and passengers were eventually disembarked with no reports of injury. Affected travelers have since been reaccommodated onto a replacement flight which was set to depart at 1:13 PM.

After nearly two decades with Southwest, N281WN was delivered to the airline in June 2007 and carries the "500th WN 737" sticker on its fuselage. The jet is configured to carry 143 passengers in an all-economy-class layout. Southwest operates an all-Boeing 737 fleet, with around 270 737-700s in service , making it the world's largest operator of the type, according to ch-aviation.

If an aircraft engine fails on takeoff, the crew will use asymmetric thrust control because the plane is likely to turn or roll toward the dead side. This means the pilots apply opposite rudder and aileron to keep the plane level and maintain control. If the crew cannot stop safely on the r unway, they will continue the takeoff , follow pre-calculated climb gradients, and declare an emergency to local air traffic control.
As the crew runs through emergency checklists, they may burn excessive fuel or dump fuel while circling back or diverting to another airport for a safe single-engine landing.
body_zh: 记者 – Aaron 是一名航空和旅行记者，在旅行和旅游业拥有 14 年的经验。他的背景涵盖机场运营、航空基础设施和旅游咨询，曾与新西兰、欧洲和北美的全球组织合作。
Aaron 将行业专业知识与五大洲超过 52 个国家/地区的第一手旅行经验相结合，涵盖航空公司、机场、航空政策和更广泛的旅行领域。他居住在新西兰坎特伯雷。
他的作品发表在《Simple Flying》上，并受到 MSN、SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel、EIN News、Pakistan Defence 和 Climate Depot 的专题报道。
周五，西南航空的一架航班从约翰·韦恩机场-奥兰治县机场 (SNA) 起飞后不久，发动机发生故障。这导致这架已使用 19 年的波音 737-700 宣布紧急状态并改飞洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX)。这架航班搭载的是该国最大的航空公司之一，停止爬升并大声鸣叫7700，这是空中交通管制一般紧急情况的标准广播。
WN3396 是从 SNA 飞往诺曼·米内塔·圣何塞国际机场 (SJC) 的定期航班，在紧急情况下改道飞往洛杉矶国际机场，并在那里安全着陆。
据 CodeThreeNews 报道，机上机组人员向空中交通管制部门证实，机上共有 97 人，在从圣安娜起飞后不久，这架飞机的 2 号发动机就失去了动力。事件中的这架飞机注册号为 N281WN，是交付给该航空公司的第 500 架波音 737。它已为这家位于达拉斯的运营商积累了超过 19 年的主动服务经验。
事件发生后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 发布了《洛杉矶时报》获得的以下声明。
“在机组人员报告发动机出现问题后，西南航空 3396 航班于当地时间中午 12 点 25 分左右安全降落在洛杉矶国际机场。”
西南航空发言人也在周五向 Simple Flying 发表的一份声明中证实了这一事件。
他们解释说：“西南航空 3396 航班在从约翰韦恩机场飞往圣何塞米内塔国际机场时，飞行员收到与发动机相关的维护指示后，安全转移到洛杉矶国际机场。” “飞行员遵循既定程序，飞机平安着陆。我们对飞行员和机组人员的专业精神表示赞赏。西南航空将为我们的乘客安排另一趟飞往圣何塞的航班。对于西南航空来说，没有什么比我们的乘客和员工的安全更重要的了。”
飞机在洛杉矶上空盘旋
根据 Simple Flying Flight Tracker 的数据，WN3396 定于 11:35 从圣安娜出发，向北快速飞行一小时飞往圣何塞。飞机最终于 11 点 49 分从登机口返回，比原计划晚了 14 分钟。
飞机向东北方向起飞后，在出现发动机问题后迅速转向西南方向，随后飞机转向西南方向飞往洛杉矶南湾。飞行数据显示，这架飞机的飞行高度从未超过 5,000 英尺（1,524 米）。飞机在太平洋上空飞行 18 分钟后，获准降落在洛杉矶国际机场，并于 12 点 28 分安全降落在 25L 跑道上，总飞行时间为 38 分钟。
紧急服务人员在飞机抵达后赶到，乘客最终下机，没有受伤报告。受影响的旅客已被重新安排乘坐原定于下午 1:13 起飞的替代航班。
与西南航空合作近二十年后，N281WN 于 2007 年 6 月交付给该航空公司，机身上贴有“第 500 架 WN 737”标签。该飞机采用全经济舱布局，可搭载 143 名乘客。据ch-aviation 称，西南航空运营着一支全波音 737 机队，约有 270 737-700 架在役，使其成为全球最大的该类型运营商。
如果飞机发动机在起飞时出现故障，机组人员将使用不对称推力控制，因为飞机可能会转向或滚向死角。这意味着飞行员使用相反的方向舵和副翼来保持飞机水平并保持控制。如果机组人员无法安全停在跑道上，他们将继续起飞，遵循预先计算的爬升梯度，并向当地空中交通管制部门宣布紧急情况。
当机组人员检查紧急检查表时，他们可能会燃烧过多的燃油或倾倒燃油，同时盘旋或转移到另一个机场以进行安全的单引擎着陆。

body_en: Florida Learjet crash: flight data and recovered elevator offer clues - Aviation24.be
Home Miscellaneous Accidents Florida Learjet crash: flight data and recovered elevator offer clues

Investigators have confirmed that part of Learjet 60 N722BD’s tail separated before it struck the ground near West Palm Beach on 1 November, killing all nine people aboard. However, whether that separation caused the loss of control or resulted from the aircraft’s rapid descent remains unresolved.

The aircraft was flying from Austin-Bergstrom, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. The NTSB identifies its operator as Aurora Aviation, trading as Upper Jet. Its latest published update, dated 5 November, confirms that wreckage recovery remains under way; no probable cause has been established.

Flightradar24’s tracking shows that the 2004-built business jet departed Austin at approximately 15:37 UTC. After cruising at higher altitude, it descended towards 35,000 feet over southern Florida, before briefly climbing and entering a steep right-hand descent at around 17:48 UTC.

The crew’s radio calls provide important context. According to NTSB briefing details reported by Aviation Week , the pilots described light clear icing, considered manageable, and moderate turbulence causing altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They subsequently reported precipitation and requested a climb to 37,000 feet. Shortly after receiving clearance, they declared an emergency, reporting a rapid descent and an overspeed condition. These are observations made by the crew, not findings that icing caused the accident.

The downloadable Flightradar24 data illustrates the descent’s severity: recorded altitude falls from 31,350 feet at 17:48:39 UTC to 8,750 feet at 17:49:23 — approximately 22,600 feet in 44 seconds. That represents an average recorded descent rate of about 30,800 feet per minute over that interval.

Crucially, these are tracking measurements, not a complete flight-recorder reconstruction. The final entries repeat 8,750 feet while position continues changing: they do not demonstrate that the aircraft levelled off. Nor should the reported groundspeed be confused with airspeed or used alone to establish an overspeed. The latter was reported separately by the crew. Source: Flightradar24’s published data .
The elevator discovery — evidence, but not yet an explanation

At the 3 November briefing, NTSB member Thomas Chapman said investigators had recovered most of the left elevator in three pieces, between approximately 2.1 and 6.1 kilometres from the impact site. The elevator is a movable tail surface used to control the aircraft’s nose-up and nose-down movement. Its recovery away from the main wreckage establishes separation before impact.

The unresolved question is the sequence. Did a control-surface failure initiate the loss of control, or did aerodynamic loads during the dive tear the elevator away? Investigators have not determined when it detached. Weather is also a key investigative focus, but neither the crew’s icing reports nor the debris distribution establishes the initiating cause.

On 5 November, the NTSB reported that excavation had begun the previous evening and that part of an engine had been found. Wreckage has also been recovered from nearby roofs and will be transferred to a secure location for examination.

Maintenance records indicated that a cockpit voice recorder had been installed, but investigators initially could not confirm whether it remained aboard. The latest official update does not announce its recovery. For now, the evidence documents an exceptionally rapid descent and an in-flight separation — not why the emergency began.

首页 其他事故 佛罗里达州里尔喷气机坠毁：飞行数据和恢复的电梯提供线索
调查人员已证实，11 月 1 日，里尔 60 N722BD 飞机在撞击西棕榈滩附近的地面之前，机尾部分分离，导致机上 9 人全部遇难。然而，这种分离是导致失控还是飞机快速下降造成的仍然悬而未决。
这架飞机从德克萨斯州奥斯汀-伯格斯特罗姆飞往巴哈马群岛的北伊柳塞拉。 NTSB 认定其运营商为 Aurora Aviation，交易名称为 Upper Jet。其最新发布的更新日期为 11 月 5 日，确认残骸打捞仍在进行中；尚未确定可能的原因。
Flightradar24 的追踪显示，这架 2004 年制造的商务飞机于世界标准时间 15:37 左右从奥斯汀起飞。在更高海拔巡航后，它在佛罗里达州南部上空下降到 35,000 英尺的高度，然后在世界标准时间 17:48 左右短暂爬升并进入陡峭的右侧下降。
机组人员的无线电呼叫提供了重要的背景信息。根据《航空周刊》报道的 NTSB 简报详细信息，飞行员描述了轻微的清晰结冰，被认为是可以控制的，以及导致高度偏差约 700 英尺的中度湍流。他们随后报告了降雨并要求爬升至 37,000 英尺的高度。在获得许可后不久，他们宣布进入紧急状态，报告了快速下降和超速情况。这些是机组人员的观察结果，而不是结冰导致事故的发现。
可下载的 Flightradar24 数据说明了下降的严重程度：记录的高度从 UTC 时间 17:48:39 的 31,350 英尺下降到 17:49:23 的 8,750 英尺——大约在 44 秒内下降了 22,600 英尺。这表示在此期间记录的平均下降率约为每分钟 30,800 英尺。
至关重要的是，这些是跟踪测量，而不是完整的飞行记录器重建。最终条目重复 8,750 英尺，同时位置不断变化：它们并不表明飞机已保持平稳。报告的地速也不应与空速混淆或单独用于确定超速。后者由机组人员单独报告。资料来源：Flightradar24 公布的数据。
电梯的发现——证据，但尚未解释
在 11 月 3 日的简报会上，国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 成员托马斯·查普曼 (Thomas Chapman) 表示，调查人员已将左侧电梯的大部分分为三块，距离撞击地点约 2.1 至 6.1 公里。升降舵是一个可移动的尾翼面，用于控制飞机的机头向上和机头向下运动。它从主残骸中恢复，在撞击前建立了分离。
未解决的问题是顺序。是控制面故障导致失控，还是潜水过程中的空气动力载荷导致升降舵脱落？调查人员尚未确定其何时分离。天气也是一个关键的调查焦点，但船员的结冰报告和碎片分布都无法确定引发原因。
11 月 5 日，国家运输安全委员会报告说，挖掘工作已于前一天晚上开始，并发现了发动机的一部分。残骸也已从附近的屋顶找到，并将被转移到安全地点进行检查。
维修记录显示驾驶舱录音机已安装，但调查人员最初无法确认它是否仍留在飞机上。最新的官方更新并没有宣布恢复。目前，证据显示飞机下降得异常迅速，并在飞行中发生分离——这并不是紧急情况开始的原因。

title_en: The Airline That Invented Premium Economy Just Built A 42-Inch Seat Nobody Else Can
title_zh: 发明高级经济舱的航空公司刚刚打造了无人能及的 42 英寸座椅
summary: When looking at premium economy offerings, there is only one airline where you can find a 42-inch seat.
summary_zh: 在查看豪华经济舱产品时，只有一家航空公司可以提供 42 英寸的座位。
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

Getting passengers in seats is the number one priority of all airlines. How an airline achieves this is usually down to routes as well as the product itself and how it differs from others in the market. Today, the most contested part of the cabin has arguably become premium economy. Global carriers are racing to capture affluent long-haul commuters, and the strategic challenge is no longer just about building a spacious seat, but deploying it where it can inflict the maximum competitive damage. EVA Air is one of the airlines that is leading the way, a pioneer of the premium economy concept, and still retaining its dominance.

The airline's recent progress signals a deeper structural shift in how boutique international airlines challenge massive legacy alliances on ultra-long-haul flight tracks. Instead of funneling travelers through crowded West Coast transit points, the focus has shifted toward capturing high-yield corporate and premium leisure demand directly from prime East Coast markets.

First, the new staple route between Taipei Taoyuan International Airport (TPE) and Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) begins a tale of aggressive expansion of intercontinental capacity. Operating four times per week, this new corridor marks the carrier's tenth North American gateway, pushing its total regional footprint to an unprecedented 98 weekly flights. By entering the US National Capital region, the airline is intentionally establishing a direct pipeline into a market that generates immense corporate, diplomatic, and premium diaspora traffic.

Skipping over traditional multi-stop routings changes the financial landscape for travelers who have spent years navigating arduous connections. In the past, more than 40,000 passengers traveling annually between the Washington metropolitan area and greater Asia had to connect through highly congested West Coast hubs, according to Travel Tourister . The new direct 7,860-mile (12,649 km) sector completely removes that friction, offering an efficient 14-hour eastbound sprint and a 15.5-hour westbound block time, to the delight of these regular travelers.

The economic ramifications of this single-route injection are massive, highlighting the high-yield value of mature transpacific corridors. According to EVA Air, the new service will generate more than $61 million in annual economic impact for the capital region while significantly shifting market-share balances. For an independent carrier operating outside the major transatlantic mega-alliances, getting a firm foothold at Dulles is an excellent way to capture elite corporate accounts that traditionally rely on domestic legacy carriers.

A route is never complete without an accompanying aircraft, and fortunately for EVA Air, the best choice is already in the fleet. The carrier chose to configure its newest batch of Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner airframes in a tightly optimized three-class layout, balancing premium margin and structural density. Total capacity is capped at 278 seats, meticulously divided into 26 Royal Laurel business class suites, 28 Premium Economy spaces, and 224 standard economy seats.

By dedicating just four rows to the premium economy environment in a spacious seven-abreast, 2-3-2 configuration, the airline is breaking firmly with the industry status quo. This cabin density lets the airline offer a generous 42-inch (106.7 cm) seat pitch, giving passengers far more personal space than competitive alternatives. Each seat incorporates an advanced cradle-motion system that slides the lower cushion forward and upward simultaneously, providing an eight-inch (20.3 cm) recline without encroaching on the passenger behind.

The cabin composition maximizes revenue potential per square foot by catering to an affluent middle market that values workspace over basic transit. Each space is loaded with utility, featuring a 15.6-inch (39.6 cm) high-definition touchscreen monitor, built-in personal electronic device holders, and dual power configurations. By choosing a lower seat count over a dense layout, the airline creates a scarce, high-demand asset that lets it maintain strong pricing integrity during both peak and shoulder travel seasons.
Getting Hooked On The Premium Economy Experience

The immediate arrival of a 42-inch (106.7 cm) product standard at Dulles heavily disrupts the traditional long-haul landscape connecting the eastern United States to East Asia. Elite regional competitors have historically maintained a highly uniform product standard on their ultra-long-haul fleets, typically capping their mid-cabin offerings at a conventional 38-inch (96.5 cm) pitch. This four-inch (10.2 cm) discrepancy creates a severe competitive deficit for legacy operators that have long relied on cabin density to maximize raw ticket volume.

Compared with the tight layout choices of alternative alliance carriers, the spatial divergence becomes clear to corporate travelers who pay close attention to every product offering. Competitors operating out of neighboring East Coast hubs often deploy an eight-abreast 2-4-2 alignment on their flagship aircraft, narrowing the cushion width available to individual passengers. Scaling down to a seven-abreast configuration on a widebody frame restores substantial shoulder room, turning a long 15-hour flight track into a manageable workspace.

Put simply, this is precisely how an independent player dictates market expectations from a single international gateway. Travelers experiencing the enhanced spatial layout quickly develop a lower tolerance for restrictive industry-standard cabins on subsequent transpacific journeys. As this route matures into the late summer season, an elite intermediate tier will force surrounding operators to re-evaluate whether their high-density configurations can truly protect their premium market shares.

Launching a direct transpacific service to the East Coast serves a clear structural purpose by shifting traffic away from traditional West Coast connecting gateways. Travelers originating in the mid-Atlantic region had to funnel through immense hubs like Los Angeles or San Francisco to reach East Asia. This extra domestic leg adds hours of travel time, heightens the risk of misplaced baggage, and introduces the fatigue of terminal transfers. Now offering a direct alternative, the carrier skips over these consolidated bottlenecks entirely and establishes a more streamlined transit corridor.
body_zh: 航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
让乘客入座是所有航空公司的首要任务。航空公司如何实现这一目标通常取决于航线、产品本身以及它与市场上其他航空公司的不同之处。如今，客舱中最具争议的部分可以说已经成为豪华经济舱。全球航空公司正在竞相吸引富裕的长途通勤者，战略挑战不再只是建造宽敞的座位，而是将其部署在能够造成最大竞争损害的地方。长荣航空是领先的航空公司之一，是高级经济舱概念的先驱，并且仍然保持着主导地位。
该航空公司最近的进展标志着精品国际航空公司在超长途航线上挑战大规模传统联盟的方式发生了更深层次的结构性转变。重点不再是通过拥挤的西海岸中转站吸引游客，而是直接从东海岸的主要市场捕捉高收益的企业和高端休闲需求。
首先，台北桃园国际机场 (TPE) 和华盛顿杜勒斯国际机场 (IAD) 之间的新主线航线开始了积极扩张洲际运力的故事。这条新走廊每周运营四趟，标志着该航空公司的第十个北美门户，将其区域​​足迹总数推至前所未有的每周 98 趟航班。通过进入美国国家首都地区，该航空公司有意建立一条进入市场的直接管道，该市场会产生巨大的企业、外交和高端侨民流量。
跳过传统的多站路线改变了多年来在艰难的转机中航行的旅行者的财务状况。据《旅游者》报道，过去，每年有超过 40,000 名旅客往返于华盛顿都市区和大亚洲地区，必须通过高度拥挤的西海岸枢纽转机。新的 7,860 英里（12,649 公里）直达航段完全消除了这种摩擦，提供高效的 14 小时东行冲刺时间和 15.5 小时西行阻塞时间，让这些常旅客感到高兴。
这种单线注入的经济影响是巨大的，凸显了成熟的跨太平洋走廊的高收益价值。据长荣航空称，这项新服务将为首都地区带来超过 6100 万美元的年度经济影响，同时显着改变市场份额平衡。对于一家在主要跨大西洋超级联盟之外运营的独立航空公司来说，在杜勒斯机场站稳脚跟是获得传统上依赖国内传统航空公司的精英企业客户的绝佳方式。
追踪天空最有趣的时刻，直播
等待、改航和稀有飞机，一目了然。免费，无需注册。
没有陪伴飞机的航线永远不会完整，幸运的是，对于长荣航空来说，最好的选择已经在机队中。该航空公司选择将最新一批波音 787-9 梦想飞机机身配置为严格优化的三舱布局，平衡溢价利润和结构密度。总容量上限为 278 个座位，精心划分为 26 个皇家桂冠商务舱套房、28 个豪华经济舱座位和 224 个标准经济舱座位。
通过在宽敞的七并排、2-3-2 布局中仅使用四排座位来打造豪华经济舱环境，该航空公司坚定地打破了行业现状。这种客舱密度使该航空公司能够提供 42 英寸（106.7 厘米）的宽敞座椅间距，为乘客提供比竞争对手更多的个人空间。每个座椅均采用先进的摇篮运动系统，可同时向前和向上滑动下部坐垫，提供 8 英寸（20.3 厘米）的倾斜度，而不会影响后面的乘客。
客舱结构迎合了重视工作空间而非基本交通的富裕中端市场，从而最大限度地提高了每平方英尺的收入潜力。每个空间都配备了实用工具，配有 15.6 英寸（39.6 厘米）高清触摸屏显示器、内置个人电子设备支架和双电源配置。通过选择较少的座位数而不是密集的布局，该航空公司创造了一种稀缺的、高需求的资产，使其能够在旅游旺季和平季保持强大的定价完整性。
沉迷于豪华经济舱体验
42 英寸（106.7 厘米）产品标准的立即抵达杜勒斯机场，严重扰乱了连接美国东部和东亚的传统长途航线格局。优秀的区域竞争对手历来在其超长途机队中保持高度统一的产品标准，通常将其中舱产品限制在传统的 38 英寸（96.5 厘米）间距。这种四英寸（10.2 厘米）的差异给长期依赖客舱密度来最大化原始机票量的传统运营商造成了严重的竞争赤字。
与其他联盟航空公司的紧凑布局选择相比，对于密切关注每项产品供应的商务旅行者来说，空间差异变得更加明显。在邻近的东海岸枢纽运营的竞争对手经常在其旗舰飞机上部署八并排的 2-4-2 排列，从而缩小了单个乘客可用的坐垫宽度。在宽体机身上缩小至七并排配置可以恢复大量的肩部空间，将长达 15 小时的飞行轨迹变成一个易于管理的工作空间。
简而言之，这正是独立参与者通过单一国际门户决定市场预期的方式。经历了增强的空间布局的旅客很快就会对随后的跨太平洋旅程中限制性的行业标准客舱产生较低的容忍度。随着这条航线在夏末逐渐成熟，精英中间层将迫使周边运营商重新评估他们的高密度配置是否能够真正保护他们的高端市场份额。
推出直达东海岸的跨太平洋服务，通过将交通从传统的西海岸连接门户转移出去，具有明确的结构性目的。来自大西洋中部地区的旅客必须经过洛杉矶或旧金山等大型枢纽才能到达东亚。这条额外的国内航线增加了旅行时间，增加了行李丢失的风险，并带来了航站楼转机的疲劳。现在，该航空公司提供了一种直接的替代方案，完全跳过了这些整合的瓶颈，并建立了一条更加精简的运输走廊。

title_en: Why The Boeing 747-400 Was A Turning Point For Two-Pilot Cockpits
title_zh: 为什么波音 747-400 是两名飞行员驾驶舱的转折点
summary: The Boeing 747-400 revolutionized jumbo-jet cockpits, replacing the flight engineer with advanced automation and a two-pilot flight deck.
summary_zh: 波音 747-400 彻底改变了大型喷气式飞机的驾驶舱，用先进的自动化和两名飞行员的驾驶舱取代了飞行工程师。
body_en: Experienced ICAO English Language Proficiency Instructor for pilots and ATCOs and conference interpreter who is passionate about facilitating effective communication within aviation-related businesses. Possess a deep understanding of the aviation industry, including aviation regulations, terminology, and industry-specific communication protocols. Has been working at numerous airshows across Europe since 2014. Being an ultralight pilot in her free time, she also promotes safety and efficiency in aviation operations.

For almost two decades, operating the Boeing 747 meant having three people on the flight deck. Alongside the captain and first officer, a dedicated flight engineer monitored the jumbo jet's complex systems, managed fuel distribution, checked engine parameters, and ensured its electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems operated correctly. But the introduction of the 747-400 changed this longstanding arrangement, demonstrating that even one of the world's largest commercial aircraft could be operated by just two pilots.

However, the 747-400 was not the first commercial aircraft to adopt a two-pilot cockpit. Boeing 757 and 767 had already demonstrated the advantages of computerized flight decks, while other manufacturers had experimented with similar arrangements on four-engine aircraft. Nevertheless, the 747-400 represented a major milestone in bringing two-pilot operations to the jumbo-jet category. How did Boeing eliminate the flight engineer, what happened to the responsibilities previously assigned to that position, and how did the change influence subsequent generations of commercial aircraft?
Why Did Earlier Boeing 747s Require Three Flight Deck Crew Members?

When the original Boeing 747 entered commercial service with Pan American World Airways on January 22, 1970, its flight deck reflected late-1960s technology. The aircraft was considerably more complex than previous commercial jetliners, featuring four engines, extensive fuel systems, multiple hydraulic circuits, and sophisticated environmental controls. As a result, Boeing designed the original 747-100 to operate with three flight deck crew members: a captain, a first officer, and a flight engineer. This arrangement continued with the subsequent 747-200 and 747-300 generations. Boeing's official 747 historical overview identifies these three aircraft as the original Classics generation.

On most aircraft, the flight engineer sat in a dedicated seat behind the two pilots , facing a large instrument panel with hundreds of switches, gauges, indicators, and circuit breakers. While the captain and first officer concentrated on flying, navigation, and communication, the flight engineer monitored the aircraft's technical condition and performed numerous operational tasks. This included checking engine performance, managing fuel transfers between tanks, monitoring electrical generators, maintaining hydraulic pressure, and controlling cabin pressurization. On a four-engine aircraft as large as the 747, these responsibilities created a considerable workload, especially during departure, cruise, and abnormal operating conditions. The Boeing 747 flight deck historical overview compares the original cockpit arrangement with its modern successor.

Importantly, the flight engineer was not an additional pilot. The position required specialist technical training and a detailed understanding of aircraft systems, allowing the two pilots to concentrate on their primary flying responsibilities. The arrangement was also common across earlier generations of four-engine commercial aircraft, including the Boeing 707 and Douglas DC-8 . However, as electronic systems became more sophisticated, aircraft manufacturers began to question whether a dedicated third crew member was still necessary. Boeing's subsequent 757 and 767 programs would answer that question.
How Did The Boeing 757 And 767 Prepare The Industry For Two-Pilot Operations?
Credit: Einar Magnus Magnusson | Shutterstock

The transition toward two-pilot commercial aircraft was already underway when Boeing began developing its 757 and 767 programs. Both aircraft entered service in the early 1980s, introducing advanced digital avionics and electronic flight displays that significantly reduced the need for conventional cockpit instrumentation. The 757 entered commercial service with Eastern Air Lines in January 1983, while the 767 followed later that year . Their integrated systems demonstrated that many functions previously requiring dedicated monitoring could be handled through computerized aircraft equipment. NASA 's historical research into cockpit automation documents the technological changes introduced with the two aircraft, showing that the development was not entirely straightforward.

Boeing initially faced regulatory and industry resistance to operating larger aircraft with only two pilots. The 1981 Presidential Task Force on Aircraft Crew Complement examined whether advanced automation could safely absorb the responsibilities traditionally assigned to flight engineers. Its findings supported two-pilot operations and helped establish the regulatory foundation for aircraft such as the 767. NASA's publication, Human Factors of Advanced Technology Aircraft , explains how Engine Indication and Crew Alerting System (EICAS) technology became central to this transition. The system was even described as an electronic flight engineer because it could monitor aircraft systems and alert pilots when intervention was necessary.

Contrary to popular belief, the Boeing 747-400 was not the first four-engine jet aircraft certified for two-pilot operation. That distinction belongs to the Lockheed JetStar , the first quadjet designed for two-pilot operation, introduced into service in 1961. Meanwhile, the British Aerospace BAe 146 , which first flew in 1981 and entered commercial service in 1983, is recognized as the first commercial passenger quadjet certified for a two-pilot flight deck. Before these developments, four-engine mainline jetliners traditionally required a flight engineer. Thus, the 747-400 did not invent the concept, but it extended that philosophy to the jumbo-jet market.
First quadjet overall with two-pilot operations
First commercial passenger quadjet certified for two-pilot operations
Extended two-pilot philosophy to the jumbo jet

Boeing already had the technological foundations in place when it decided to modernize its flagship aircraft. However, transferring the concept to the 747 required a much more extensive redesign than simply removing the flight engineer's seat.
How Did Boeing Automate the Flight Engineer On The 747-400?
body_zh: 经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。
近二十年来，操作波音 747 意味着飞行甲板上需要三个人。除了机长和副驾驶之外，一名专门的飞行工程师还负责监控这架大型喷气式飞机的复杂系统，管理燃油分配，检查发动机参数，并确保其电气、液压和气动系统正常运行。但 747-400 的推出改变了这一长期的安排，表明即使是世界上最大的商用飞机之一也可以仅由两名飞行员操作。
然而，747-400并不是第一架采用两名飞行员驾驶舱的商用飞机。波音 757 和 767 已经展示了计算机化驾驶舱的优势，而其他制造商也在四引擎飞机上尝试了类似的安排。尽管如此，747-400 仍然是大型喷气式飞机类别中引入两名飞行员操作的一个重要里程碑。波音公司是如何取消飞行工程师的，之前分配给该职位的职责发生了什么变化，以及这一变化如何影响后续几代商用飞机？
为什么早期的波音 747 需要三名驾驶舱机组人员？

当最初的波音 747 于 1970 年 1 月 22 日开始在泛美世界航空公司投入商业运营时，其飞行甲板体现了 20 世纪 60 年代末的技术。该飞机比以前的商用喷气式飞机复杂得多，具有四个发动机、广泛的燃油系统、多个液压回路和复杂的环境控制装置。因此，波音公司将最初的 747-100 设计为由三名驾驶舱机组人员运行：一名机长、一名副驾驶和一名飞行工程师。随后的 747-200 和 747-300 几代延续了这种安排。波音公司的官方 747 历史概述将这三架飞机视为最初的经典一代。

在大多数飞机上，飞行工程师坐在两名飞行员后面的专用座位上，面对一个带有数百个开关、仪表、指示器和断路器的大型仪表板。当机长和副驾驶专注于飞行、导航和通信时，飞行工程师监控飞机的技术状况并执行大量操作任务。这包括检查发动机性能、管理油箱之间的燃油传输、监控发电机、维持液压以及控制机舱增压。在像 747 这样大的四引擎飞机上，这些职责造成了相当大的工作量，特别是在起飞、巡航和异常操作条件下。波音 747 驾驶舱历史概述将原始驾驶舱布置与其现代后继者进行了比较。
重要的是，飞行工程师不是额外的飞行员。该职位需要专业的技术培训和对飞机系统的详细了解，使两名飞行员能够专注于他们的主要飞行职责。这种布置在早期几代四引擎商用飞机中也很常见，包括波音 707 和道格拉斯 DC-8。然而，随着电子系统变得更加复杂，飞机制造商开始质疑是否仍然需要专门的第三名机组人员。波音公司随后推出的 757 和 767 项目将回答这个问题。
波音 757 和 767 如何让业界为两名飞行员操作做好准备？
图片来源：Einar Magnus Magnusson | Shutterstock

当波音公司开始开发 757 和 767 项目时，向两名飞行员商用飞机的过渡已经开始。这两架飞机均于 20 世纪 80 年代初投入使用，引入了先进的数字航空电子设备和电子飞行显示器，大大减少了对传统驾驶舱仪表的需求。 757 于 1983 年 1 月在东方航空投入商业运营，767 也于同年晚些时候投入商业运营。他们的集成系统表明，以前需要专门监控的许多功能可以通过计算机化的飞机设备来处理。美国宇航局对驾驶舱自动化的历史研究记录了这两架飞机引入的技术变革，表明发展并不完全简单。

波音公司最初因运营只有两名飞行员的大型飞机而面临监管和行业阻力。 1981 年，总统飞机机组人员特别工作组研究了先进的自动化是否能够安全地承担传统上分配给飞行工程师的职责。其研究结果支持两名飞行员操作，并帮助为 767 等飞机奠定了监管基础。NASA 的出版物《先进技术飞机的人为因素》解释了发动机指示和机组警报系统 (EICAS) 技术如何成为这一转变的核心。该系统甚至被描述为电子飞行工程师，因为它可以监控飞机系统并在需要干预时向飞行员发出警报。

与普遍看法相反，波音 747-400 并不是第一架获得两名飞行员操作认证的四引擎喷气式飞机。这一荣誉属于洛克希德捷星 (Lockheed JetStar)，它是第一架专为两名飞行员操作而设计的四喷气式飞机，于 1961 年投入使用。与此同时，英国航空航天公司 BAe 146 于 1981 年首飞，并于 1983 年进入商业服务，被认为是第一架获得两名飞行员驾驶舱认证的商业客运四喷气式飞机。在这些发展之前，四引擎干线喷气式客机传统上需要一名飞行工程师。因此，747-400 并未发明这一概念，但它将这一理念扩展到了大型喷气式飞机市场。
第一架配备两名飞行员操作的四轴喷气式飞机
首架经过两名飞行员操作认证的商用四机喷气机
将两名飞行员的理念扩展到大型喷气式飞机
当波音决定对其旗舰飞机进行现代化改造时，它已经具备了技术基础。然而，将这一概念转移到 747 上需要进行更广泛的重新设计，而不仅仅是拆除飞行工程师的座椅。

title_en: 5 Qantas Boeing 787-9 Routes Longer Than 8,000 Miles
title_zh: 5 条澳洲航空波音 787-9 航线，长度超过 8,000 英里
summary: Examining the ultra-long-haul portfolio of Australia's flag carrier in 2026.
summary_zh: 审视 2026 年澳大利亚旗舰航空公司的超远程航线组合。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Qantas runs the most demanding Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner network in the world today. Five routes flown by the airline's Dreamliners stretch beyond 8,000 miles, and the longest of them, Perth to London, has needed a Singapore fuel stop westbound since Middle East airspace closures forced longer flight paths. This countdown ranks the five by great circle distance, from Perth to Rome at about 8,300 miles (13,357 km) up to Perth to London at 9,010 miles (14,500 km).

Qantas flight QF5 took off from Perth on the night of June 22, 2022. Qantas had not flown to Rome since 2003, back when it operated multi-stop Boeing 747 services via cities like Singapore and Bangkok. While initially launched in response to surging post-pandemic summer holiday crowds, the business profile of QF5/QF6 has evolved into a highly resilient asset.

The route covers about 8,300 miles (13,357 km), and the westbound leg lasts 16 hours and 25 minutes. It is roughly 700 miles (1,126 km) shorter than Perth to London, and thus is the only route on this list that allows the 787-9 to carry a truly full load of passengers and cargo. QF5 has also remained fully nonstop in both directions despite other long-haul itineraries being forced to use layovers since Russia closed its airspace in 2022.

The flying season spans roughly six months from Spring to Fall and, thanks to exceptional demand, the service has carried well over 70,000 passengers since its inception. Qantas relies on connections in Perth to allow travelers from the east coast of Australia to step off a domestic flight and board a Rome-bound Dreamliner. More than 50% of the route’s passengers come from Australia's eastern cities: Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane.

The Auckland (AKL) to New York (JFK) corridor is one of the most intensely contested and economically vital battlegrounds in modern ULH aviation. It operates over a distance of 8,828 miles (14,207 km). Historically, traffic connecting Australia and New Zealand to the East Coast of the US relied on multi-stop journeys via West Coast gateways like Los Angeles (LAX) or San Francisco (SFO). Today, the route operates as a fierce, high-stakes duopoly between Qantas (QF3/QF4) and its cross-Tasman rival, Air New Zealand (NZ2/NZ1).

Air New Zealand initially pioneered the nonstop air bridge in 2022. Qantas launched New York flights on June 14, 2023, after a gap of more than three years, using Auckland as the stop in place of LAX, meeting Air New Zealand head-on. Spanning nearly 14,200 kilometers, the flight time regularly stretches between 16 hours and 17.5 hours, heavily dictated by severe high-altitude jet streams shifting across the Pacific Ocean. This extreme distance places intense operational constraints on Qantas’ 787-9.
Perth Airport (PER) – Rome Fiumicino Airport (FCO)
Auckland Airport (AKL) – John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK)
Perth Airport (PER) – Paris Charles De Gaulle Airport (CDG)
Melbourne Airport (MEL) – Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW)
Perth Airport (PER) – London Heathrow Airport (LHR)

Data shows that only 33% of the flight’s total passenger load originates in Sydney. The remaining two-thirds of the cabin is dynamically fed by passengers funneling from other Australian hubs, predominantly Brisbane and Melbourne , alongside local New Zealand flyers. The route relies heavily on top-tier premium business travel during the week, capturing finance, technology, and corporate executives moving between the financial districts of Sydney, Melbourne, and Manhattan. On weekends, the traffic shifts toward high-end premium leisure travelers.

In order to safely undertake the long trans-Pacific sortie, the 787-9 must trade some of its payload for fuel before taking off. That requires the Qantas business model to maximize appeal to higher-paying customers like business travelers and drop some of its seating capacity in the economy section. It has proven to be a highly lucrative asset, capturing an exceptionally high average load factor of 84% for Qantas. Owing to its popularity, QF3/QF4 operates Monday to Friday with weekend service during surges.

Qantas began nonstop flying from Perth to Paris in July 2024, making history by establishing the first nonstop twinjet service between Australia and France. Australian Aviation reported that the inaugural QF33 flight was scheduled for 17 hours and 20 minutes. The route covers 8,863 miles (14,263 km), a little shorter than London but well past the 787-9's full payload range.

The route immediately injected 75,000 annual seats into the Europe–Australia market. Prior to this service, Qantas had not touched down in the French capital since 2004, when it retired its aging Boeing 747-400 multi-stop service via Singapore. In the years that passed, like its sister route to London (QF9), the Perth–Paris sector has become a major case study in adapting to complex international geopolitics.

In response to volatile Middle East airspace closures, Qantas had to dynamically reroute flights to ensure absolute passenger safety. While the route was initially engineered to be a strict nonstop, Qantas shifted its operational strategy for the westbound Perth-to-Paris leg to include a technical and commercial stopover at Singapore Changi Airport (SIN). Rather than treating the Singapore detour as a pure operational penalty, Qantas masterfully converted it into a commercial victory.

QF33 relies on capturing top-tier 'Kangaroo Route' market share away from Middle Eastern airlines. By permanently re-routing the service via Singapore, Qantas expanded overall Paris network frequencies from three weekly flights up to five. Exactly like the Rome service, this flight officially originates at Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (SYD), but concurrently, Qantas boosted feeder flights between Perth and Singapore. The air bridge has thrived in spite of obstacles and commands premium prices from travelers eager to avoid a middle-of-the-night stopover in the Gulf.

Melbourne Airport's chief executive called it the longest route ever flown from the city when Qantas started Melbourne to Dallas/Fort Worth flights in December 2022. It was also the fourth longest in the world at the time, according to Airways. The airline framed the mission as a companion to its existing Sydney to Dallas flights, and it even flies the same 787-9 with 236 seats, split into 42 business, 28 premium economy, and 166 economy.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
澳洲航空运营着当今世界上要求最严格的波音 787-9 梦想客机网络。该航空公司的梦想客机有 5 条航线，飞行里程超过 8,000 英里，其中最长的航线是珀斯飞往伦敦，由于中东空域关闭迫使航线更长，西行需要在新加坡加油。此倒计时按大圆距离对前五名进行排名，从珀斯到罗马的距离约为 8,300 英里（13,357 公里），珀斯到伦敦的距离为 9,010 英里（14,500 公里）。
澳洲航空 QF5 航班于 2022 年 6 月 22 日晚从珀斯起飞。澳洲航空自 2003 年以来就没有飞往罗马，当时该公司运营经新加坡和曼谷等城市的多站波音 747 航班。虽然最初是为了应对疫情后暑假人群激增而推出的，但 QF5/QF6 的业务概况已发展成为一种高度弹性的资产。
路线全长约 8,300 英里（13,357 公里），西行行程持续 16 小时 25 分钟。该航线比珀斯飞往伦敦的航线短约 700 英里（1,126 公里），因此是此列表中唯一允许 787-9 真正满载乘客和货物的航线。尽管自 2022 年俄罗斯关闭领空以来，其他长途航线被迫中转，但 QF5 仍保持双向完全不间断。
飞行季节从春季到秋季大约持续六个月，由于需求旺盛，该服务自推出以来已运送了超过 70,000 名乘客。澳洲航空依靠珀斯的转机，让来自澳大利亚东海岸的旅客下了国内航班，登上飞往罗马的梦想飞机。该航线超过50%的乘客来自澳大利亚东部城市：悉尼、墨尔本和布里斯班。

奥克兰 (AKL) 至纽约 (JFK) 走廊是现代 ULH 航空中竞争最激烈、经济最重要的战场之一。它的运营距离为 8,828 英里（14,207 公里）。从历史上看，连接澳大利亚和新西兰与美国东海岸的交通依赖于通过洛杉矶 (LAX) 或旧金山 (SFO) 等西海岸门户的多站旅程。如今，这条航线在澳洲航空 (QF3/QF4) 及其跨塔斯曼竞争对手新西兰航空 (NZ2/NZ1) 之间形成激烈、高风险的双寡头垄断。
新西兰航空于 2022 年首次开创了直达空中桥梁。时隔三年多，澳洲航空于 2023 年 6 月 14 日开通了纽约航班，以奥克兰作为洛杉矶国际机场的经停点，与新西兰航空正面交锋。航程近 14,200 公里，飞行时间通常在 16 至 17.5 小时之间，这在很大程度上受到太平洋上猛烈高空急流的影响。这种极端的距离给澳洲航空的 787-9 带来了严格的运营限制。
珀斯机场 (PER) – 罗马菲乌米奇诺机场 (FCO)
奥克兰机场 (AKL) – 约翰·肯尼迪国际机场 (JFK)
珀斯机场 (PER) – 巴黎戴高乐机场 (CDG)
墨尔本机场 (MEL) – 达拉斯/沃斯堡国际机场 (DFW)
珀斯机场 (PER) – 伦敦希思罗机场 (LHR)
数据显示，该航班仅载客总量的33%是从悉尼出发的。剩下的三分之二的机舱由来自澳大利亚其他枢纽（主要是布里斯班和墨尔本）的乘客以及新西兰当地的乘客提供动态供给。该航线在很大程度上依赖于本周的顶级高端商务旅行，吸引在悉尼、墨尔本和曼哈顿金融区之间移动的金融、技术和企业高管。周末，客流转向高端休闲旅客。
为了安全地进行长途跨太平洋飞行，787-9 必须在起飞前用部分有效载荷换取燃料。这要求澳洲航空的商业模式最大限度地吸引商务旅客等高付费客户，并减少经济舱的部分座位容量。事实证明，它是一项利润丰厚的资产，为澳洲航空带来了 84% 的极高平均载客率。由于其受欢迎程度，QF3/QF4 周一至周五运营，高峰时段提供周末服务。
澳洲航空于 2024 年 7 月开始从珀斯飞往巴黎的直飞航班，通过建立澳大利亚和法国之间的首个直飞双喷气机服务创造了历史。澳大利亚航空报道称，QF33 首航预计飞行 17 小时 20 分钟。该航线全长 8,863 英里（14,263 公里），比伦敦短一点，但远远超出了 787-9 的满载航程。
该航线立即为欧洲-澳大利亚市场注入了75,000个年度座位。在此之前，澳洲航空自 2004 年退役其老化的波音 747-400 经新加坡多站航班以来，就没有在法国首都降落过。在过去的几年里，与通往伦敦的姐妹航线（QF9）一样，珀斯-巴黎航线已成为适应复杂国际地缘政治的主要案例。
为了应对不稳定的中东空域关闭，澳洲航空必须动态地改变航班航线，以确保乘客的绝对安全。虽然该航线最初被设计为严格的直达航线，但澳洲航空改变了西行珀斯至巴黎航线的运营策略，包括在新加坡樟宜机场 (SIN) 进行技术和商业中途停留。澳洲航空并没有将新加坡绕行视为纯粹的运营惩罚，而是巧妙地将其转化为商业胜利。
QF33 依赖于从中东航空公司手中夺取顶级“袋鼠航线”市场份额。通过永久性地将航班改道经新加坡，澳洲航空将整个巴黎网络的班次从每周 3 趟航班增加到 5 趟。与罗马航班一样，该航班正式从悉尼金斯福德·史密斯机场 (SYD) 起飞，但与此同时，澳洲航空增加了珀斯和新加坡之间的支线航班。尽管困难重重，这座空中桥梁仍然蓬勃发展，并为渴望避免在海湾地区半夜中途停留的旅客收取了高价。
墨尔本机场首席执行官称，当澳洲航空于 2022 年 12 月开通墨尔本飞往达拉斯/沃斯堡的航班时，这是有史以来从该城市起飞的最长航线。据航空公司称，该航线当时也是世界上第四长的航线。该航空公司将该任务视为其现有悉尼至达拉斯航班的配套航班，甚至还使用同样的 787-9 飞机，共有 236 个座位，分为 42 个商务舱座位、28 个豪华经济舱座位和 166 个经济舱座位。

title_en: When Is An Airport Lounge Visit Not Worth It? Here’s How I Decide…
title_zh: 什么时候不值得去机场休息室？这就是我的决定……
summary: Airport lounges used to be a quiet escape from the terminal. Now they're often the most crowded spot, so here's how I decide when a visit is worth it.
summary_zh: 机场休息室曾经是远离航站楼的安静场所。现在它们通常是最拥挤的地方，所以以下是我如何决定何时值得一游。
body_en: It goes without saying that a lot about the passenger experience when traveling by air has changed over the decades, both for better and worse. I think perhaps one of the most fascinating transformations we’ve seen over the years involves airport lounges, and how their purpose has completely flipped.

I’d like to talk about that in a bit more detail in this post, and share my approach to using lounges. Let me emphasize that there are of course all kinds of lounges out there , from international first class lounges , to international business class lounges , to Priority Pass, membership, and credit card lounges . This post is primarily about lounges that fall into that last category, in terms of being pretty widely accessible.
The purpose of airport lounges has shifted massively

Look, I’m not trying to sound like some boomer talking about how things were in “the good old days” (nothing against boomers… hi, dad!), but I think it’s interesting to compare how things were 15-20 years ago, to how they are today.

Back in the day, airport lounges — even the most basic ones — were primarily about escaping the hustle and bustle of the terminal, and having a quiet place from which to work, with free Wi-Fi and easy access to charging ports. At the time, free Wi-Fi and charging ports in terminals were incredibly rare. The food in most standard domestic lounges sucked — it was typically cubed cheese, snack mix, and not a whole lot else.

It also goes without saying that lounges were mostly very poorly monetized. Airport real estate is incredibly expensive, and lounges were primarily a cost center for their operators, as part of an overall value proposition for travelers.

Fast forward to today, and look at the state of lounges in the United States. Lounges have much better food than they used to, and they also have much better amenities than they used to. Also, exponentially more people have access to the lounges than they used to. They’re actually pretty nice destinations in airports.

The catch is that they’ve completely lost their initial purpose — they’re no longer a place you go to escape the crowds, and quite to the contrary, they’re often the most crowded place in a terminal . In many lounges you’ll find every single seat occupied, and even a very long waitlist to get in.

Obviously this is great for monetization, since lounge operators maximize their return by having the lounges utilized as much as possible, so that the cost can be divided by the highest number of people possible. Ironically, we’ve also seen terminals largely get much nicer over the years. It’s nowadays common to see free Wi-Fi and charging ports throughout terminals, and it’s usually not too hard to just find a quiet place to sit, with more peace than you’d find in a lounge.
What’s your approach to using airport lounges?

Back in the day, if I had lounge access, my obvious move was always to use the lounge if I had time. I mean, that seems like a pretty obvious move, right? After all, you get access to something “premium,” so you want to make the most of it. Most people with TSA PreCheck don’t say “meh, you know, I think I’ll skip that today and go through the regular line.”

At the same time, I think one has to step back and look at things objectively. At times it almost feels like people use lounges religiously in order to justify the annual fees on their credit cards, and so they can talk about how they’re eating for “free.”

You’ll often see people on social media essentially call airport lounges upper middle class airport cafeterias, and that’s probably not actually too far off in terms of how they’re practically used… and there’s nothing wrong with that!
Personally, for places with consistently crowded lounges, my approach to lounge use is pretty straightforward
I’ll visit the lounge if I want to eat or drink something (though I’m usually not very hungry at airports, and I’m also not looking to guzzle alcohol)
Then when I’m done, I’ll typically just head toward my gate, and stop at any gate area that looks relatively empty, and sit there until close to boarding time

Honestly, this is one of the reasons I really love grab & go lounges, where you can pick up something to take with you. To me that’s the ideal setup, since it serves the purpose I’m actually looking for from lounges — if a lounge is going to be crowded, I’d rather just be able to grab what I’d like, and head somewhere quiet.

As someone who loves coffee , it’s why I also appreciate when lounges have great coffee to go. It’s typically the item I most want to consume at airports, and the wait for a cup of coffee at an airport can often be quite long early in the morning.
The lounge crowding issue nowadays is only made worse by the number of people who are watching videos and making calls with no headphones in lounges.

The whole concept of airport lounges has changed massively over the years. Monetization of lounges has largely gotten better, as they’ve become a key component of the credit card race that we’re seeing between airlines and card issuers.
body_zh: 不言而喻，几十年来，乘客乘飞机旅行的体验发生了很多变化，有好有坏。我认为，也许我们多年来看到的最令人着迷的转变之一涉及机场休息室，以及它们的用途如何完全转变。
我想在这篇文章中更详细地讨论这一点，并分享我使用休息室的方法。我要强调的是，当然有各种各样的休息室，从国际头等舱休息室，到国际公务舱休息室，到Priority Pass、会员卡、信用卡休息室。这篇文章主要是关于属于最后一类的休息室，因为它的使用范围相当广泛。
机场休息室的用途发生了巨大转变
听着，我并不是想让自己听起来像某个婴儿潮一代谈论“过去的美好时光”（没有反对婴儿潮一代的意思……嗨，爸爸！），但我认为将 15-20 年前的情况与今天的情况进行比较很有趣。
过去，机场休息室（即使是最基本的休息室）主要是为了逃离航站楼的喧嚣，拥有一个安静的工作场所，提供免费 Wi-Fi 和方便的充电端口。当时，航站楼内的免费 Wi-Fi 和充电端口非常罕见。大多数标准国内休息室的食物都很糟糕——通常是奶酪块、零食混合物，没有其他任何东西。
不言而喻的是，休息室的盈利能力大多都很差。机场房地产非常昂贵，而休息室主要是其运营商的成本中心，作为旅客整体价值主张的一部分。
快进到今天，看看美国的休息室状况。休息室的食物比以前好得多，而且设施也比以前好得多。此外，进入休息室的人数也比以前多了很多。它们实际上是机场中非常不错的目的地。
问题是它们已经完全失去了最初的目的——它们不再是一个逃离人群的地方，相反，它们往往是航站楼中最拥挤的地方。在许多休息室，您会发现每个座位都被占用，甚至还有很长的候补名单。
显然，这对于货币化非常有利，因为休息室运营商通过尽可能多地利用休息室来最大化其回报，从而可以将成本除以尽可能多的人数。具有讽刺意味的是，多年来我们也看到终端在很大程度上变得更好。如今，在整个航站楼内随处可见免费 Wi-Fi 和充电端口，而且通常不难找到一个安静的地方坐下来，比在休息室里更安静。
您使用机场休息室的方法是什么？
过去，如果我可以使用休息室，我的明显举动总是在有时间的情况下使用休息室。我的意思是，这似乎是一个非常明显的举动，对吧？毕竟，您可以获得一些“优质”的东西，因此您想充分利用它。大多数接受 TSA PreCheck 的人不会说“嗯，你知道，我想我今天会跳过这个，走常规通道。”
与此同时，我认为人们必须退后一步，客观地看待事物。有时，人们似乎虔诚地使用休息室，以证明信用卡年费的合理性，这样他们就可以谈论他们如何“免费”吃饭。
你经常会在社交媒体上看到人们基本上将机场休息室称为中上阶层机场自助餐厅，就其实际使用方式而言，这实际上可能并不太遥远……这并没有什么问题！
就我个人而言，对于休息室持续拥挤的地方，我使用休息室的方法非常简单
如果我想吃点东西或喝点东西，我会去休息室（尽管我在机场通常不会很饿，而且我也不想酗酒）
然后，当我完成后，我通常会朝登机口走去，并在任何看起来相对空旷的登机口区域停下来，坐在那里直到接近登机时间
老实说，这是我非常喜欢“Grab & Go”休息室的原因之一，在那里你可以拿起一些东西随身携带。对我来说，这是理想的设置，因为它满足了我实际上在休息室寻找的目的——如果休息室很拥挤，我宁愿能够拿走我想要的东西，然后前往安静的地方。
作为一个热爱咖啡的人，这就是为什么我也很喜欢休息室提供美味的咖啡。它通常是我在机场最想消费的东西，而在机场等待一杯咖啡往往会在清晨等待很长时间。
如今，越来越多的人在休息室不戴耳机观看视频和打电话，这使得休息室拥挤问题变得更加严重。
多年来，机场休息室的整体概念发生了巨大变化。休息室的货币化在很大程度上得到了改善，因为它们已成为航空公司和发卡机构之间信用卡竞赛的关键组成部分。

title_en: Why The Pilatus PC-24 Can Land On Grass Runways Most Private Jets Cannot
title_zh: 为什么皮拉图斯 PC-24 可以在大多数私人飞机无法降落的草地跑道上降落
summary: Most private jets need paved runways. The Pilatus PC-24 was built around a very different idea, and the reason starts beneath the fuselage.
summary_zh: 大多数私人飞机需要铺设跑道。 Pilatus PC-24 是围绕一个非常不同的想法构建的，其原因始于机身下方。
body_en: Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

Park a typical business jet beside a wet grass strip, and its crew will probably look for another airport. A jet engine inhales air at tremendous speed, so a loose stone or a splash of mud can turn a routine landing into a six-figure repair. But one Swiss twinjet has been formally approved to do exactly what its rivals avoid. According to Pilatus , the Pilatus PC-24 is certified for takeoffs and landings on grass, wet soil, dry sand, gravel, and snow-covered unpaved runways.

That sounds like a brochure line until you read the certification record. The real question is not whether a PC-24 can touch down on turf once, in perfect weather, but how Pilatus convinced regulators to approve it as normal operation. The answer involves a flooded English field, a snowy test site in northern Canada, a specific main-wheel pressure, and a design decision taken years before the first prototype flew. But first, why do almost all of its rivals stay on the pavement?

The short answer is that they were built that way on purpose. As we explained here, most business jets are optimized for efficiency, speed, and comfort on paved runways, while unpaved operations demand reinforced landing gear and specialized tires that add weight. Modifying a finished design to cope would be expensive and impractical. We also noted that turbofans are less forgiving than propeller aircraft when it comes to foreign object damage , the industry term for debris sucked into an engine.

Grass adds problems that pavement never poses. A wet turf strip can lengthen braking distances, ruts and soft patches can punish the nose and main gear, and a hidden stone is invisible from the cockpit. For a pilot of a conventional jet, every one of those variables is a reason to divert. For an engineer, each one is a design requirement that must be met before the first landing, not after.

There are exceptions, but they come with asterisks. According to the same report, the Dassault Falcon 20 and Falcon 50 can land on dirt and gravel after being fitted with a special service bulletin kit, yet neither was originally designed for it. The PC-24 started from the opposite direction. Pilatus says the jet was developed for rough-field use from the outset, a mindset inherited from its PC-12 turboprop, and the company markets it as the “Super Versatile Jet.” That distinction matters more than it sounds. A jet that can be coaxed onto a grass strip by a brave crew is one thing; a jet whose manufacturer has proven the maneuver to aviation authorities is another. So what did that proof actually look like?
How Pilatus Certified The PC-24 For Rough-Field Operations

It took two stages. Pilatus first obtained certification for dry sand and gravel in 2018, then spent all of 2019 on a post-certification test campaign. In a media release dated February 7, 2020 , the company announced full rough-field approval, adding grass, wet soil, and snow-covered unpaved runways. As reported by AOPA in its coverage of the PC-24's expanded rough-field certification , European regulators approved the aircraft's expanded unpaved-runway capabilities, with US approval following. This gave the eight-seat jet access to a much wider network of airports. According to Pilatus' own technical brochure , the PC-24 can access almost twice as many airports worldwide as competing business jets, thanks largely to its ability to operate from unpaved runways.

The EASA requires certification tests to be flown on different surfaces, so Pilatus took the jet across two continents. Business Jet Traveler listed the grass-runway sites as Goodwood and Duxford in England, Kunovice in the Czech Republic and Poitiers in France. According to our previous report , engineers also flooded an English field with about 45,000 US gallons (170,000 liters) of water to mimic rain of roughly 0.16 inches (4 mm) per hour, and the PC-24 coped. In the Czech Republic, crews rehearsed single-engine take-offs, engine failures and the loss of ground spoilers and anti-skid, with heavy rain adding to the challenge.

Wet soil was arguably the hardest case. Pilatus says the Woodbridge site in England required complex conditions to be reproduced in part, just to meet every specification for take-offs and landings on wet dirt. The company also took the jet to Kuujjuaq, Canada, for snow-covered gravel, a surface where visibility, drag and braking all change at once.

Passing a braking test was only part of the job. Engineers also wanted to know what the surface did to the airplane: whether snow packed into the flaps, whether stones reached the engines, whether brakes and steering held up. Nothing was ingested by the engines and the jet performed better than expected. Which raises the obvious follow-up: what did Pilatus build into the aircraft to make that possible?
The PC-24 Uses Specialized Landing Gear For Grass Runways

The PC-24 uses long-stroke trailing-link landing gear that smooths out uneven ground, and its main tires run at 73-76.5 psi (5-5.24 bar) so the aircraft does not sink into soft surfaces. A trailing link hangs each wheel from a pivoting arm, so the wheel can rise and fall over a bump without hammering the airframe. The logic behind the tire pressure is the same as snowshoes: lower pressure spreads weight across a larger footprint, which matters when the aircraft weighs up to 18,700 pounds (8,500 kg) at takeoff.

Then comes the engine problem. The two Williams FJ44-4A turbofans, each producing about 3,400 pounds of thrust (15 kN), sit high on the rear fuselage, far from the stones and spray the wheels throw up. The same report adds that the wing flaps shield the engines from debris. During the Canadian trials, one prototype carried instrumentation and cameras to show whether snow or slush built up on the flaps, fuselage or landing gear, so engineers could compare the impact with dry gravel.

Braking was a separate question. According to our previous report, Pilatus asked whether steering was affected, whether the brakes were sufficient, and how the anti-skid system behaved on loose surfaces. Those details determine whether a crew can stop a fast, heavy aircraft on a surface that gives way underfoot, and we checked them through inspections and recorded data rather than assuming them. Rugged feet are only half of a rough-field jet. The other half is the wing, and it hides the most counterintuitive trick in the design. How does an airplane that cruises at 440 knots arrive so slowly?
The PC-24 Combines 440-Knot Speed With Short-Field Performance
body_zh: 安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
将一架典型的公务机停在潮湿的草地旁边，其机组人员可能会寻找另一个机场。喷气发动机以极快的速度吸入空气，因此一块松动的石头或一滴泥土就可以将例行着陆变成六位数的维修费用。但瑞士的一架双发喷气式飞机已被正式批准，可以做其竞争对手所避免做的事情。据皮拉图斯介绍，皮拉图斯 PC-24 经过认证，可在草地、湿土、干沙、砾石和积雪覆盖的未铺砌跑道上起飞和降落。
在您阅读认证记录之前，这听起来像是一本小册子。真正的问题不是 PC-24 能否在完美的天气下在草坪上着陆一次，而是皮拉图斯如何说服监管机构批准其正常运行。答案涉及一片被洪水淹没的英国田野、加拿大北部的一个白雪皑皑的测试场地、特定的主轮压力以及第一架原型机飞行前几年做出的设计决策。但首先，为什么几乎所有竞争对手都停留在人行道上？
简而言之，它们是故意这样建造的。正如我们在此解释的，大多数公务机都针对铺砌跑道上的效率、速度和舒适度进行了优化，而未铺砌的运行则需要加固的起落架和会增加重量的专用轮胎。修改已完成的设计来应对这种情况将是昂贵且不切实际的。我们还注意到，在异物损坏（行业术语是指吸入发动机的碎片）方面，涡轮风扇发动机比螺旋桨飞机更不宽容。
草增加了人行道不会带来的问题。潮湿的草皮条会延长制动距离，车辙和软斑会损害机头和主起落架，而驾驶舱内看不见隐藏的石头。对于传统喷气式飞机的飞行员来说，这些变量中的每一个都是改道的原因。对于工程师来说，每一项都是必须在第一次着陆之前满足的设计要求，而不是之后。

也有例外，但它们带有星号。根据同一份报告，达索猎鹰 20 和猎鹰 50 在安装特殊服务公告套件后可以在泥土和砾石上着陆，但这两种飞机最初都不是为此设计的。 PC-24从相反的方向出发。皮拉图斯表示，这款喷气式飞机从一开始就是为野外使用而开发的，这种理念继承自 PC-12 涡轮螺旋桨飞机，该公司将其营销为“超级多功能喷气式飞机”。这种区别比听起来更重要。一架喷气式飞机可以被勇敢的机组人员哄到草地上是一回事；另一回事是另一回事。制造商已向航空当局证明其机动性的喷气式飞机是另一种情况。那么这个证明实际上是什么样的呢？
Pilatus 如何认证 PC-24 适合野外作业

这需要两个阶段。 Pilatus 于 2018 年首次获得干砂和砾石认证，然后在 2019 年全年进行认证后测试活动。在 2020 年 2 月 7 日的媒体发布中，该公司宣布了全面的粗糙场地批准，增加了草地、湿土和积雪覆盖的未铺砌跑道。正如 AOPA 在其关于 PC-24 扩展野外认证的报道中所报道的那样，欧洲监管机构批准了该飞机扩展的未铺砌跑道能力，美国随后也批准了该飞机。这使得这架八座喷气式飞机能够进入更广泛的机场网络。根据皮拉图斯自己的技术手册，PC-24 可以访问的全球机场数量几乎是竞争对手公务机的两倍，这主要归功于它能够在未铺砌的跑道上运行。

EASA 要求在不同表面进行飞行认证测试，因此皮拉图斯驾驶这架飞机穿越了两大洲。 Business Jet Traveler 将草地跑道地点列为英格兰的古德伍德和达克斯福德、捷克共和国的库诺维采和法国的普瓦捷。根据我们之前的报告，工程师还向英国的一块田地注入了约 45,000 美制加仑（170,000 升）的水，以模拟每小时约 0.16 英寸（4 毫米）的降雨，PC-24 也能应对。在捷克共和国，机组人员演练了单引擎起飞、引擎故障以及地面扰流板和防滑装置的丢失，而大雨又增加了挑战。
潮湿的土壤可以说是最困难的情况。皮拉图斯表示，英国伍德布里奇机场需要部分复制复杂的条件，以满足在湿土上起飞和着陆的所有规格。该公司还将这架飞机飞往加拿大库朱阿克，前往冰雪覆盖的砾石路面，那里的能见度、阻力和制动都会同时发生变化。
通过制动测试只是工作的一部分。工程师们还想知道表面对飞机的影响：雪是否挤进了襟翼，石头是否到达了发动机，刹车和转向系统是否正常。发动机没有吸入任何东西，飞机的性能比预期的要好。这就提出了明显的后续问题：皮拉图斯在飞机中内置了什么以使这成为可能？
PC-24 使用草地跑道专用起落架
PC-24 使用长冲程后连杆起落架，可以平滑不平坦的地面，其主轮胎的运行压力为 73-76.5 psi（5-5.24 bar），因此飞机不会陷入柔软的表面。尾连杆将每个轮子悬挂在枢转臂上，因此轮子可以在颠簸处上升和下降，而不会敲击机身。轮胎压力背后的逻辑与雪鞋相同：较低的压力将重量分散到较大的足迹上，当飞机起飞时重量高达 18,700 磅（8,500 公斤）时，这一点很重要。
然后是发动机问题。两台威廉姆斯 FJ44-4A 涡轮风扇发动机，每台可产生约 3,400 磅推力（15 kN），高高地安装在机身后部，远离石头并喷射车轮扬起的水花。同一份报告还补充说，襟翼可以保护发动机免受碎片的影响。在加拿大的试验期间，一架原型机携带仪器和摄像机来显示襟翼、机身或起落架上是否积雪或雪泥，以便工程师可以将其影响与干燥砾石进行比较。
制动是一个单独的问题。根据我们之前的报道，皮拉图斯询问了转向是否受到影响，刹车是否足够，以及防滑系统在松软路面上的表现如何。这些细节决定了机组人员是否能够在脚下塌陷的地面上阻止一架快速重型飞机，我们通过检查和记录数据来检查它们，而不是假设它们。坚固的脚只是越野喷气式飞机的一半。另一半是机翼，它隐藏着设计中最违反直觉的技巧。一架以 440 节巡航速度的飞机为何到达速度如此之慢？
PC-24 将 440 节速度与短场性能相结合

title_en: Delta Air Lines Boosts Summer 2027 Schedule With New Routes & Expanded Weekend Frequencies
title_zh: 达美航空推出新航线并扩大周末班次，提高 2027 年夏季航班时刻表
summary: Delta expands its summer 2027 leisure network as strong 2026 load factors support returning routes and additional weekend flights.
summary_zh: 由于 2026 年强劲的客座率支持返程航线和额外的周末航班，达美航空扩大了 2027 年夏季休闲网络。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

Delta Air Lines has announced another expansion of its summer 2027 network, featuring 11 seasonal routes, additional weekend frequencies on five domestic services, and increased flying to 10 Latin American and Caribbean destinations. The changes announced today target leisure travelers heading to mountain resorts, national parks, and beach destinations.

The strategy builds on Delta's summer 2026 expansion, which introduced Saturday-only flights from Austin Bergstrom International Airport (AUS) and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) alongside returning seasonal services elsewhere. Analysis of newly available Department Of Transportation (DOT) data reveals that numerous routes achieved load factors exceeding 90%, explaining why Delta is maintaining its focus on weekend leisure demand while selectively increasing capacity.
Delta Brings Back 11 Seasonal Routes For Summer 2027

Delta's latest announcement features 11 routes originating from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW), Austin and Los Angeles. All appeared in the airline's original summer 2026 plans , with destinations including Bozeman, Kalispell, Jackson Hole and Pensacola.

Most services begin in late May or June, although flights to Bangor will continue into October, extending beyond the traditional summer vacation period. Importantly, Detroit–Destin represents a reinstatement, having been canceled before summer 2026 operations began.

While a once-weekly service might seem thin, it taps into leisure travelers who want to get away for a week and seek new destinations. This travel segment has surged post-pandemic , and Delta is betting that the trend will continue in 2027.
Amy Martin, Delta's Vice President of Network Planning, spoke about the latest expansion.

“We’re continuing to tailor Delta’s schedule around where our customers want to travel. By adding weekend flights to some of the most sought-after leisure destinations, we’re giving customers more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their summer.”

The airline is also including eight previously loaded Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) routes, serving destinations such as Charleston, Savannah and Halifax, alongside two Florida connections from LaGuardia Airport (LGA). These additions complement Delta's wider Boston expansion, which includes new European connections for 2027.
How Did Delta's Summer 2026 Leisure Routes Perform?

The return of these routes suggests that Delta found success with them this past summer, and analysis of the DOT's T-100 data indicates this was definitely the case. Detroit–Pensacola achieved the highest June-July 2026 average load factor at 95.5%, followed by Atlanta-Bangor at 92.2% and Atlanta-Rapid City at 91.5%. Detroit-Bangor and Detroit-Bozeman also performed strongly, averaging approximately 89%, suggesting particularly robust demand from established Delta hubs.

However, newer routes didn't perform at those levels, with Austin-Bozeman, Austin-Kalispell, and Los Angeles-Jackson Hole all operating below 80% full. Nevertheless, Delta has already extended Austin-Bozeman into winter, when it will operate daily during peak ski season. Such decisions illustrate why summer occupancy alone cannot determine profitability or a route's longer-term potential.

Delta is also increasing capacity on five established domestic routes, adding a weekend frequency to each. The changes include Orlando and Fort Myers service from Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport (CVG), beginning in April, while Minneapolis–Kalispell receives more flying from June. These enhancements suggest Delta is selectively investing in established markets alongside its returning leisure experiments.
Delta Targets Caribbean & Latin America Growth As Well

International leisure expansion forms another major component of Delta's plans. 10 routes across Latin America and the Caribbean will receive additional Saturday frequencies, extended operating seasons, or both. Atlanta accounts for half, with the airline highlighting a new Saturday flight to St. Lucia that will improve connections through its largest hub.

Delta's latest expansion consequently emphasizes refining existing networks rather than introducing large numbers of entirely new destinations. Strong 2026 load factors on several routes help explain the strategy, though the return of slightly weaker performers suggests other considerations, including seasonal yields and aircraft utilization. With fuel costs encouraging greater capacity discipline, targeted weekend flying lets Delta pursue leisure growth without substantial year-round commitments.
body_zh: Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍布 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
达美航空宣布再次扩大其 2027 年夏季网络，新增 11 条季节性航线、增加 5 条国内航班的周末班次，并增加飞往 10 个拉丁美洲和加勒比目的地的航班。今天宣布的这些变化针对的是前往山区度假胜地、国家公园和海滩目的地的休闲旅行者。
该战略建立在达美航空 2026 年夏季扩张的基础上，该计划推出了仅周六从奥斯汀伯格斯特罗姆国际机场 (AUS) 和洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX) 出发的航班，以及其他地方的季节性返程航班。对交通部 (DOT) 最新数据的分析显示，许多航线的载客率超过 90%，这解释了达美航空为何在有选择地增加运力的同时继续关注周末休闲需求。
达美航空将于 2027 年夏季恢复 11 条季节性航线
达美航空最新宣布开通 11 条从亚特兰大哈茨菲尔德-杰克逊国际机场 (ATL)、底特律大都会韦恩县机场 (DTW)、奥斯汀和洛杉矶出发的航线。所有这些都出现在该航空公司最初的 2026 年夏季计划中，目的地包括博兹曼、卡利斯佩尔、杰克逊霍尔和彭萨科拉。
大多数航班于五月下旬或六月开始，但飞往班戈的航班将持续到十月，超出传统的暑假期间。重要的是，底特律-德斯廷航线代表着在 2026 年夏季运营开始之前被取消的航班的恢复。
虽然每周一次的服务可能看起来很薄弱，但它吸引了那些想要离开一周并寻找新目的地的休闲旅行者。这一旅行领域在疫情后激增，达美航空押注这一趋势将在 2027 年持续下去。
达美航空网络规划副总裁艾米·马丁 (Amy Martin) 谈到了最新的扩展。
“我们将继续根据客户想去的地方调整达美航空的航班时刻表。通过增加飞往一些最受欢迎的休闲目的地的周末航班，我们为客户提供了更大的灵活性和更多的方式来充分利用他们的夏季。”
该航空公司还包括之前开通的 8 条波士顿洛根国际机场 (BOS) 航线，服务于查尔斯顿、萨凡纳和哈利法克斯等目的地，以及两条从拉瓜迪亚机场 (LGA) 出发的佛罗里达航线。这些新增航线补充了达美航空在波士顿的更广泛扩张，其中包括 2027 年新增的欧洲航线。
达美航空 2026 年夏季休闲航线表现如何？
这些航线的回归表明达美航空在去年夏天在这些航线上取得了成功，对交通部 T-100 数据的分析表明情况确实如此。底特律 - 彭萨科拉在 2026 年 6 月至 7 月期间实现了最高的平均载客率，达到 95.5%，其次是亚特兰大 - 班戈 (92.2%) 和亚特兰大 - 拉皮德城 (91.5%)。底特律-班戈和底特律-博兹曼也表现强劲，平均约为 89%，表明达美航空枢纽的需求特别强劲。
然而，较新的航线并没有达到这样的水平，奥斯汀-博兹曼、奥斯汀-卡利斯佩尔和洛杉矶-杰克逊霍尔的运营率均低于 80%。尽管如此，达美航空已经将奥斯汀-博兹曼航线延长至冬季，并在滑雪旺季期间每天运营。这些决定说明了为什么夏季入住率本身无法决定盈利能力或航线的长期潜力。
达美航空还增加了 5 条已建立的国内航线的运力，并为每条航线增加了周末班次。这些变化包括从 4 月开始从辛辛那提北肯塔基国际机场 (CVG) 出发的奥兰多和迈尔斯堡航班，而明尼阿波利斯-卡利斯佩尔从 6 月起接收更多航班。这些改进表明达美航空在回归休闲实验的同时，有选择性地投资于成熟市场。
达美航空也瞄准了加勒比海和拉丁美洲的增长
国际休闲扩张是达美航空计划的另一个重要组成部分。横跨拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的 10 条航线将增加周六班次、延长运营季节，或两者兼而有之。亚特兰大占一半，该航空公司强调周六飞往圣卢西亚的新航班将改善其最大枢纽的连接。
因此，达美航空最新的扩张强调完善现有网络，而不是引入大量全新的目的地。 2026 年多条航线的强劲载客率有助于解释这一战略，尽管表现稍弱的航线的回归表明了其他考虑因素，包括季节性收益率和飞机利用率。由于燃油成本鼓励加强运力控制，有针对性的周末飞行让达美航空无需全年做出大量承诺即可追求休闲增长。

title_en: The Airport Spending $335 Million So Connecting Passengers Stop Clearing Security Twice
title_zh: 机场斥资 3.35 亿美元让转机旅客不再两次通过安检
summary: Spokane Airport is investing millions in a new Central Hall to connect three concourses, consolidate security and eliminate repeat screening by 2030
summary_zh: 斯波坎机场正在投资数百万美元建造新的中央大厅，以连接三个大厅，巩固安全并在 2030 年之前消除重复检查
body_en: Experienced ICAO English Language Proficiency Instructor for pilots and ATCOs and conference interpreter who is passionate about facilitating effective communication within aviation-related businesses. Possess a deep understanding of the aviation industry, including aviation regulations, terminology, and industry-specific communication protocols. Has been working at numerous airshows across Europe since 2014. Being an ultralight pilot in her free time, she also promotes safety and efficiency in aviation operations.

Spokane International Airport (GEG) is preparing for one of the most significant transformations in its history, but passengers will have to endure several years of disruption before experiencing the benefits. A major portion of the airport's main terminal curbside closed on October 21, 2026, forcing motorists onto a temporary two-lane bypass road that is expected to remain in place until 2030. Inside the terminal, baggage claim facilities are also being relocated, while construction crews prepare the site for a new 255,000-square-foot building.

Central Hall is the project's centerpiece and is a $335 million project that will fundamentally change how passengers navigate GEG. The development is intended to eliminate the need for connecting passengers to leave the secure area and clear security again when transferring between concourses. But why has Spokane's existing terminal layout created this problem, and how will the airport maintain operations during such extensive reconstruction? The answers lie in its ambitious Terminal Renovation and Expansion (TREX) program.
Why GEG's Current Layout Creates Problems For Connecting Passengers

Spokane International Airport's existing terminal configuration has a significant limitation that many passengers might not immediately recognize: its concourses do not provide the seamless post-security connections available at many larger airports. Travelers transferring between certain areas of the airport may have to leave the secure area and undergo TSA screening again before reaching their next departure gate. This unnecessarily complicates connecting itineraries, especially when passengers have limited time between flights.

The problem stems from the physical separation between Concourse C and the main terminal complex serving Concourses A and B. Although passengers can move between these areas using existing terminal infrastructure, the current arrangement does not provide the fully integrated airside circulation that Spokane wants to introduce. The airport's official TREX development plans identify the Central Hall as the solution, bringing together security screening, baggage claim, and passenger circulation in a centralized facility.

For airlines, the existing arrangement can also complicate the passenger experience when itineraries involve connections between different concourses. Travelers must account for extra walking, potential security queues, and the time needed to re-enter the secure area. While Spokane is not among the largest connecting hubs in the United States , improving these arrangements could make the airport considerably more convenient for passengers traveling through the Inland Northwest. The question is how a single new building can resolve a problem that has existed across several different terminal areas.
What Is The $335 Million Central Hall Designed To Change?

The 255,000-square-foot Central Hall will become the heart of Spokane International Airport's redesigned terminal. The estimated $335 million development is the centerpiece of Phase 2 of the TREX program and will consolidate security screening and baggage claim operations. According to the Spokane Journal of Business , the project will introduce a centralized security checkpoint serving all airlines, alongside a post-security connection linking Concourses A, B, and C.

This is a major change from the airport's current setup. Instead of requiring passengers to navigate separate security areas, the Central Hall will provide one consolidated screening facility through which departing passengers can access the different concourses. After passing through security, travelers can move between concourses without returning to the terminal's public side. The building will also consolidate baggage claim facilities, creating a more straightforward arrivals experience and improving access to airport concessions and other passenger amenities.

This project is intended to provide a more intuitive terminal layout, reducing the need for passengers to understand the airport's separate concourse arrangements. Airport CEO Dave Haring has described the development as offering the most significant improvement to passenger efficiency through consolidated screening services. As reported by KHQ , Haring has also emphasized the objective of giving passengers "one place to go."

Both departing and arriving passengers will benefit from these improvements, although the new building will require substantial preparation before its construction can progress. That work has already started, and the first visible consequences are being felt outside the terminal, where the airport has had to introduce a completely different traffic arrangement.
Why Has Spokane Airport Closed Its Main Terminal Curbside Until 2030?

Building the Central Hall requires more than demolishing existing passenger facilities and building a replacement. Crews must first relocate important underground utilities, including water, sewer, and gas infrastructure, to prepare the site for the new building. This work has brought construction activity directly into the area around the main terminal, forcing Spokane International Airport to reorganize vehicle access.

On October 21, 2026, a substantial portion of the main terminal's curbside area was closed to vehicles and pedestrians. All vehicle traffic is now being directed through a newly constructed two-lane bypass road, which is expected to remain operational until 2030. According to The Spokesman-Review , the airport previously had three inbound traffic lanes, so the temporary configuration reduces capacity for vehicles entering the terminal area.

This bypass is intended to maintain access to the airport while construction crews work in the area previously occupied by the terminal's main approach roads. However, the reduced number of lanes could create additional congestion during peak departure and arrival periods. Passengers will need to follow updated signage to locate the available drop-off and pickup areas, while pedestrians using the parking facilities must access the terminal through the sky bridges. The airport has warned travelers to allow extra time for their journeys, particularly during busy periods.
body_zh: 经验丰富的国际民航组织飞行员和空中交通管制员英语语言能力讲师以及会议口译员，热衷于促进航空相关业务中的有效沟通。对航空业有深入的了解，包括航空法规、术语和行业特定的通信协议。自 2014 年以来，她一直在欧洲各地的众多航展上工作。作为一名超轻型飞行员，她在业余时间还致力于提高航空运营的安全性和效率。
斯波坎国际机场 (GEG) 正在为其历史上最重大的变革之一做准备，但乘客在体验到好处之前必须忍受数年的干扰。机场主航站楼路边的大部分区域于 2026 年 10 月 21 日关闭，迫使驾车者走上一条临时的双车道绕行道路，该道路预计将保留到 2030 年。航站楼内的行李提取设施也正在搬迁，而施工人员正在为建造一座 255,000 平方英尺的新建筑做准备。
中央大厅是该项目的核心，耗资 3.35 亿美元，将从根本上改变乘客乘坐银娱的方式。该开发旨在消除转机乘客在大厅之间转机时离开安全区域并再次通过安检的需要。但为什么斯波坎现有的航站楼布局会造成这个问题？在如此大规模的重建过程中，机场将如何维持运营？答案就在于其雄心勃勃的航站楼改造和扩建 (TREX) 计划。
为何银娱目前的布局对旅客转接造成问题
斯波坎国际机场现有的航站楼配置有一个重大限制，许多乘客可能不会立即意识到：其大厅不提供许多大型机场所提供的无缝安检后连接。在机场某些区域之间转机的旅客可能必须离开安全区域并再次接受 TSA 检查，然后才能到达下一个登机口。这不必要地使转机行程变得复杂，尤其是当乘客的航班之间的时间有限时。
问题源于 C 大厅和为 A 和 B 大厅服务的主航站楼综合体之间的物理隔离。尽管乘客可以使用现有的航站楼基础设施在这些区域之间移动，但当前的安排并未提供斯波坎想要引入的完全集成的空侧循环。机场的官方 TREX 开发计划将中央大厅确定为解决方案，将安全检查、行李领取和旅客流通集中在一个集中设施中。
对于航空公司而言，当行程涉及不同大厅之间的转机时，现有的安排也会使乘客体验变得复杂。旅客必须考虑额外的步行、潜在的安检队列以及重新进入安全区域所需的时间。虽然斯波坎不是美国最大的转机枢纽之一，但改进这些安排可以使机场为穿越西北内陆的乘客提供更大的便利。问题是一座新建筑如何解决多个不同航站楼区域都存在的问题。
耗资 3.35 亿美元的中央大厅旨在改变什么？
255,000 平方英尺的中央大厅将成为斯波坎国际机场重新设计的航站楼的核心。预计耗资 3.35 亿美元的开发项目是 TREX 计划第二阶段的核心部分，将整合安全检查和行李提取业务。据《斯波坎商业杂志》报道，该项目将引入一个为所有航空公司提供服务的集中安全检查站，以及连接 A、B 和 C 大厅的安检后连接。
这是与机场当前设置相比的重大变化。中央大厅将提供一个统一的安检设施，不再要求乘客通过单独的安检区域，出发的乘客可以通过该设施进入不同的大厅。通过安检后，旅客可以在大厅之间移动，而无需返回航站楼的公共区域。该建筑还将整合行李提取设施，创造更简单的抵达体验，并改善机场特许经营和其他乘客设施的使用。
该项目旨在提供更直观的航站楼布局，减少乘客了解机场单独大厅安排的需要。机场首席执行官戴夫·哈林 (Dave Haring) 表示，这一开发项目通过综合安检服务极大地提高了乘客效率。据 KHQ 报道，哈林还强调了为乘客提供“一个可以去的地方”的目标。
出发和到达的乘客都将从这些改进中受益，尽管新建筑在施工之前需要进行大量准备工作。这项工作已经开始，第一个明显的后果是在航站楼外感受到的，机场不得不引入完全不同的交通安排。
为什么斯波坎机场在 2030 年之前关闭其主航站楼路边？
建造中央大厅需要的不仅仅是拆除现有的客运设施并建造替代设施。工作人员必须首先重新安置重要的地下设施，包括供水、下水道和天然气基础设施，为新建筑准备场地。这项工程将施工活动直接带入主航站楼周围区域，迫使斯波坎国际机场重新组织车辆通道。
2026 年 10 月 21 日，主航站楼的大部分路边区域禁止车辆和行人通行。所有车辆交通现在都通过一条新建的两车道绕行道路进行引导，预计该道路将一直运营到 2030 年。据《发言人评论》报道，机场此前有 3 条入境车道，因此临时配置减少了进入航站楼区域的车辆通行能力。
这条旁路的目的是在施工人员在之前被航站楼主要引道占据的区域工作时保持通往机场的通道。然而，车道数量的减少可能会在出发和到达高峰期造成额外的拥堵。乘客需要按照更新的标牌找到可用的下车和上车区域，而使用停车设施的行人必须通过天桥进入航站楼。机场已警告旅客留出额外时间出行，尤其是在繁忙时期。

Home Lufthansa Group Brussels Airlines Brussels Airlines introduces Diane von Furstenberg amenity kits

Brussels Airlines is introducing amenity kits designed by Diane von Furstenberg for long-haul Business Class passengers from mid-November 2026, combining the Belgian-American designer’s signature prints with toiletries from a Belgian family-owned business.

The pouches come in two shapes and feature two DVF patterns: Vintage Weave, originally created in 1973, and Ikat, dating from the early 1980s. Each kit also includes a DVF sleep mask and toiletries supplied by Antwerp-based Waterl’eau.

Thibaut Dewilde, Brussels Airlines’ Head of Inflight Management, said the collaboration brings together an internationally recognised designer and a smaller Belgian business to showcase Belgian products on board.
The kits will be available exclusively in Business Class on the airline’s long-haul services.

Allegiant Air Trims Its Winter Schedule By 25 Routes

Las Vegas-based Allegiant Air is a US budget airline that offers no-frills, nonstop flying to destinations across the United States. The carrier has no international service and solely relies on the domestic US market. With a fleet of more than 120 aircraft, these are mixed between the Airbus A319 , A320 and Boeing 737 MAX 7 and MAX 8-200.

Reviewing historical flight schedules for 2025 and 2026, and comparing them to this winter's schedule, the airline has shaved 25 routes in total, with November seeing three routes absent from its network, including Myrtle Beach (MYR) to Niagara Falls (IAG), Phoenix (PHX) to Asheville (AVL), and Sarasota (SRQ) to Portsmouth (PSM).

The cuts don't stop there; Bellingham (BLI) to Los Angeles (LAX), Nashville (BNA) to Peoria (PIA), Cincinnati (CVG) to Los Angeles, and Las Vegas (LAS) to Boise (BOI) have disappeared for this coming January. summary_zh: 随着途易航空更广泛的业务实力增强，途易航空比利时计划在 2027 年夏季将座位容量增加 3%，增加从布鲁塞尔出发的四个目的地
body_en: TUI Airline grows capacity and adds four Brussels routes in summer 2027 - Aviation24.be

TUI fly Belgium plans to increase seat capacity by 3% for summer 2027, adding four destinations from Brussels as the wider TUI Airline business strengthens flight-only sales and seeks to make more efficient use of its aircraft.

The programme presented at a press briefing in Brussels on 6 November envisages around 1.9 million one-way seats and approximately 11,000 one-way flights, with flight numbers increasing by 4% compared with summer 2026. The Belgian network will comprise 54 routes serving 49 destinations, supported by a fleet of 19 aircraft.

The additions are Billund in Denmark, Ljubljana in Slovenia, and the Moroccan cities of Essaouira and Fez. All four routes will depart from Brussels Airport. The presentation highlighted Billund’s association with LEGOLAND, alongside the expansion of the airline’s city and leisure offering in Europe and Morocco.

TUI also plans more flights to established holiday markets, including the Canary Islands, Palma de Mallorca, Alicante, Reus, Crete, Kos, Rhodes, Madeira, Marrakech and Agadir. Launch dates and frequencies for the new routes were not specified in the slides.

The presentation by TUI Airline Chief Commercial Officer Peter Glade and TUI BeNe Region Managing Director Arjan Kers underlined a commitment to Brussels and Ostend as the airline’s Belgian bases. Its wider network comparison lists Antwerp as a base closure relative to summer 2026. Capacity changes—including increases, reductions and withdrawals—will affect 36% of the Belgian operation’s summer 2026 routes.

The Belgian programme forms part of a broader transformation of TUI Airline from a transport provider for the group’s holiday business into an airline with greater commercial responsibility of its own. The slides describe 2025–2027 as a three-year commercialisation programme, leading towards a unified profit-and-loss framework from 2028.

As early bookings tend to disappear, flight-only sales are central to that strategy. TUI is bringing together distribution, network planning and revenue management, while harmonising products and fare families across its airline operations. The presentation highlights a cross-airline distribution engine on TUIfly.com, dedicated management of flight-only inventory and greater coordination between independently sold seats and those allocated to package holidays.

TUI says it has established a commercial team and introduced a new network-planning approach for summer 2027. Its objective is to develop an airline that is profitable in its own right while continuing to support and differentiate the group’s holiday products.
More productive aircraft and a reshaped network

Across TUI Airline (the 10th-largest European airline with 133 aircraft, among which 18 Boeing 787 Dreamliners), the May–October 2027 programme provides for 17 million outbound seats, up 4.6% against the planned summer 2026 programme, and approximately 42,000 flights, up 4.1%. It includes 25 new routes and 11 new destinations.

The group intends to expand proven profitable routes, withdraw from weaker markets where it has a limited presence and reduce triangular routings. Better aircraft utilisation, particularly outside the peak summer period, is another priority. Capacity changes will affect 32% of the existing network overall.

Wider network highlights include a twice-weekly Boeing 787 service between Düsseldorf and Curaçao, alongside new Amsterdam links to Praia and Kilimanjaro. Those Amsterdam services are planned in combination with Sal and Zanzibar, respectively.

In the Netherlands , TUI’s fleet plan envisages replacing six Boeing 737-8s with seven 737-10s, with Amsterdam identified as the type’s launch base from the second quarter of 2027. The Dutch programme targets around 15% more seats per aircraft. In the UK, Gatwick is identified as the largest growth base.
For Belgium , the strategy translates into measured capacity growth and a broader Brussels offering, within a group-wide effort to improve aircraft productivity and strengthen commercial performance.

body_zh: TUI 航空公司扩大运力并于 2027 年夏季增加 4 条布鲁塞尔航线 - Aviation24.be
TUI 飞行比利时计划在 2027 年夏季将座位容量增加 3%，增加从布鲁塞尔出发的四个目的地，因为更广泛的途易航空业务加强了纯航班销售，并寻求更有效地利用其飞机。
该计划于 11 月 6 日在布鲁塞尔举行的新闻发布会上公布，预计将有约 190 万个单程座位和约 11,000 个单程航班，航班数量较 2026 年夏季增加 4%。比利时网络将包括 54 条航线，服务于 49 个目的地，并由 19 架飞机组成的机队提供支持。
新增的城市包括丹麦的比隆、斯洛文尼亚的卢布尔雅那以及摩洛哥的索维拉和非斯。所有四条航线均从布鲁塞尔机场出发。该演讲强调了比隆与乐高乐园的合作，以及该航空公司在欧洲和摩洛哥的城市和休闲服务的扩张。
TUI还计划增加飞往成熟度假市场的航班，包括加那利群岛、马略卡岛帕尔马、阿利坎特、雷乌斯、克里特岛、科斯岛、罗德岛、马德拉岛、马拉喀什和阿加迪尔。幻灯片中没有具体说明新航线的启动日期和频率。
TUI 航空公司首席商务官 Peter Glade 和 TUI BeNe 地区董事总经理 Arjan Kers 的演讲强调了将布鲁塞尔和奥斯坦德作为该航空公司的比利时基地的承诺。其更广泛的网络比较将安特卫普列为相对于 2026 年夏季关闭的基地。运力变化（包括增加、减少和撤出）将影响该比利时运营公司 2026 年夏季 36% 的航线。
比利时计划是 TUI 航空公司从集团假日业务的运输提供商转变为自身承担更大商业责任的航空公司更广泛转型的一部分。这些幻灯片将 2025-2027 年描述为一个为期三年的商业化计划，从 2028 年开始实现统一的损益框架。
由于提前预订往往会消失，仅航班销售是该策略的核心。 TUI 将分销、网络规划和收入管理整合在一起，同时协调其航空公司运营中的产品和票价系列。该演示重点介绍了 TUIfly.com 上的跨航空公司分销引擎、对纯航班库存的专门管理以及独立销售的座位与分配给套餐假期的座位之间的更好协调。
TUI表示，它已经建立了一个商业团队，并为2027年夏季推出了新的网络规划方法。其目标是发展一家能够自行盈利的航空公司，同时继续支持和差异化该集团的假日产品。
生产力更高的飞机和重塑的网络
TUI 航空公司（欧洲第十大航空公司，拥有 133 架飞机，其中 18 架波音 787 梦想飞机），2027 年 5 月至 10 月计划提供 1,700 万个出境座位，比计划的 2026 年夏季计划增加 4.6%，航班数量约为 42,000 个，增加 4.1%。其中包括25条新航线和11个新目的地。
该集团打算扩大已证明有利可图的航线，退出其业务有限的疲软市场，并减少三角航线。更好的飞机利用率，特别是在夏季高峰期之外，是另一个优先事项。容量变化将影响现有网络整体的 32%。
更广泛的网络亮点包括杜塞尔多夫和库拉索岛之间每周两班的波音 787 航班，以及阿姆斯特丹至普拉亚和乞力马扎罗的新航线。这些阿姆斯特丹服务计划分别与萨尔和桑给巴尔结合。
在荷兰，TUI 的机队计划设想用 7 架 737-10 取代 6 架波音 737-8，并从 2027 年第二季度起将阿姆斯特丹确定为该机型的发射基地。荷兰计划的目标是每架飞机增加约 15% 的座位。在英国，盖特威克被认为是最大的增长基地。
对于比利时来说，该战略转化为可衡量的运力增长和更广泛的布鲁塞尔产品，并在整个集团范围内努力提高飞机生产率和加强商业绩效。
